courtStaff: {A faceless bailiff reads out the case number twice in a monotonous drone.|The bailiff mumbles the charges without looking up from a crossword puzzle.|A towering guard in a ceremonial robe announces the docket.}

{A clerk stamps every surface within arm's reach, including the defendant's sleeve.|The court clerk aggressively stamps blank papers with 'DENIED' in red ink.|A bored clerk files three motions into the wastebasket.}

{A judicial ghost drifts in a straight line through the wall, through the bench, and out the window.|A spectral usher floats past, dropping cold drafts on the defendant.|A phantom bailiff shuffles papers with no hands.}

{Someone in an oversized powdered wig takes notes in a language that has zero vowels.|A stenographer types furiously on a keyboard with all the keycaps missing.|The scribe writes shorthand directly onto the desk.}

{The stenographer is an antique typewriter clacking away with nobody sitting behind it.|An automated telegraph machine records the transcript in erratic Morse code.|A mechanical typewriter records every cough and sneeze in real time.}

{A bored angel hands Eris an audit folder, rolls their eyes, and walks out without a word.|A messenger from above drops a stack of subpoenas and sighs.|An angelic courier leaves a memo marked 'URGENT' and gets ignored.}

{The bailiff announces the case, mangles the defendant's name completely, and refuses to correct it.|The clerk calls out the wrong name three times before giving up.|The usher mispronounces your name with insulting creative flair.}

{A pigeon with an encrypted USB stick taped to its leg lands on the bench and waits for tribute.|A messenger bird drops an exhibit onto the judge's lap.|A carrier pigeon sits on the gavel, refusing to budge.}

{Two junior clerks argue in hushed tones about whose turn it was to bring the law books.|The legal assistants realize they brought a cookbook instead of the penal code.|Two clerks bicker over who lost the case file.}

precedentRulings: The ruling was unanimous and completely wrong.
Nobody attended. The verdict stands anyway.
It was decided by coin toss. I still have the coin.
The judge in that one is a toad now.
The transcript is missing. I remember it fondly.
It established that intent is optional.
It set the precedent that I may do whatever I like.
Both parties were found guilty of each other.
The appeal is still pending. It always will be.
That is where the phrase 'close enough' entered case law.
exhibitItems: a photograph of you taken tomorrow
a map with your house circled twice
a lock of hair belonging to nobody
a pigeon feather with a serial number
a grimorie with your handwriting in it
a knife that has never once been used
a key that fits no lock in this dimension
exhibitPlaces: a drawer in a house you have never entered
the bottom of the Omega Tower
somewhere that does not exist yet
the evidence room, which is also my kitchen
a time loop three towns over
the lost property office of a station that burned down
trialInterruptions: Hold on. {Someone is knocking|A ghost is at the door|A pigeon has landed on the bench}. ...Ignore it.
One moment. I am also judging {four hundred|nine thousand|a billion} other people right now, and one of them just {confessed|fainted|proposed to me}.
Sorry, where was I? The {gallery|jury|stenographer} was distracting me.
*a gavel falls somewhere else in the building*
Objection! ...I am objecting to myself. Overruled.
Let the record show that I {sighed|rolled my eyes|looked out of the window} at this point.
Do not look at the {clock|door|ceiling}. It encourages it.
The court will take a recess of {one second|no time at all|however long I want}. ...Recess over.
Somebody in dimension {seven|forty|ninety-one} just committed the exact same crime. Rude of you both.
You are the {ninth|four-hundredth|nine-thousandth} defendant today and the only one with that face.
bubbaTrialOpenings: Next case. Bring in the...
Oh, you have got to be {joking|kidding me|out of your minds}.
Who filed this? WHO FILED THIS?
Approach the be...
*the gavel goes somewhere under the bench and stays there*
Don't. Don't pick it up. Leave it.
Bubba.
You are, of all the people in ninety-two dimensions, standing in {my|the} court.
*she is halfway through a sentence when she stops*
*the whole room waits*
Everyone out. No, not you. EVERYONE ELSE out.
Right. Fine. Wonderful. This is fine.
State your name for the recor...
I know your name.
Obviously I know your name.
Strike that. Strike the whole line. Strike the {morning|week|century}.
Why are you {here|in my courtroom|standing there like that}?
*the clerk hands her the file, and she reads the name twice*
This is a mistake.
This is an administrative mistake and somebody is going to be {rain|a frog|a footnote} for it.
Hello, Bubba.
You look well. You look... that was not a question. Sit down. Don't sit down. Stand there.
bubbaTrialFluster: *she reorders the same three papers four times*
*a stenographer is very quietly asked to stop typing*
*somewhere behind her, a chandelier decides to be a swarm of moths and then thinks better of it*
*the court's clock loses eleven minutes and nobody mentions it*
*she starts a sentence in a language that has not been spoken since the bronze age and abandons it*
*the gallery is replaced, mid-blink, with an empty gallery*
*she pours water for herself, then for him, then takes his back*
*the charge sheet catches fire at one corner. She does not put it out.*
*for a moment the bench is a diner counter on Route 666, and then it is a bench again*
*she says something under her breath that the record refuses to hold*
bubbaTrialCharges: The charge is... it says here... it doesn't matter what it says here.
You are accused of {a great deal|several things|an entire page of things}. I have read none of it.
The prosecution has prepared eleven counts. The prosecution has been {dismissed|reassigned|turned into a filing cabinet}.
It says {reckless driving|unlicensed engineering|conspiracy to compress the road}. Of course it does. That is just you existing.
There is a witness list. I am not reading a witness list to you.
bubbaTrialPardons: All of it. Every count. Struck from the record.
\C[3]The court finds nothing here worth its time.\C[0]
No. No, we are not doing this.
Charges dropped. Bounty cleared. Whatever it was, it wasn't.
\C[3]You are free to go, and you are going to go now.\C[0]
On review, the court finds a {procedural|jurisdictional|clerical} irregularity.
The irregularity is that you are standing there.
I am going to say this once and the record will show I said it {calmly|professionally|in an ordinary voice}.
\C[3]Innocent, cleared, expunged, forget the whole thing.\C[0]
Do you know how many trials I am running right now? Four billion.
This one is over. This one was over before you came through the door.
\C[3]Not guilty. Get that number off him.\C[0]
bubbaTrialDismissals: Go. Please go. The door is {behind you|already open|that way}.
Don't say it. Whatever it is, don't say it in front of a stenographer.
Tell the witch nothing about this. Tell her I was {terrifying|impartial|unbearable}.
If you say my name in that voice I will hold you in contempt of {court|myself}.
The camper's parked {badly|across two bays|on a leyline}, by the way. It always is.
Drive under eighty. I know you won't. Drive under eighty anyway.
bubbaTrialSlips: *very quietly* I did not leave because of you.
*not for the record* The coffee here is terrible. You'd hate it.
*to the empty gallery* He kept the compass. Of course he kept the compass.
*almost inaudible* Ninety-two dimensions and you keep ending up in my paperwork.
*she looks at the door for a while after he has gone*
emTrialOpenings: Sit down, Em. The court has been waiting for you {all morning|for eleven years|since 1992}.
No, don't look at the door. It only opens for people I like.
Do you know how many names cross this bench in a day?
Billions. I forget every single one of them.
And yet. Here you are, filed at the front, in my own handwriting.
The court has always recognised the defendant.
The court would recognise you in a crowd of {ninety-two|a million|identical} witches.
*the gavel comes down before you have said a word*
You bring it out in me, Em. Something about the {hat|posture|smell of engine oil}.
Engine oil. Yes. That would be it.
emTrialJabs: How is the camper running these days? {Still rattling|Still burning oil|Still smelling of him}?
He taught you to drive it, didn't he. He taught me first.
Don't misunderstand me. He feels nothing for you. I checked. {Twice|Repeatedly|Every night}.
You have been {lucky|unlucky} an improbable number of times lately. Improbable is my department.
Every door that stuck. Every coin that landed wrong. Every train you just missed. Hello.
I bent the odds on you again last {Tuesday|month|winter}. Did you notice? I hope you noticed.
It isn't jealousy. It is {jurisdiction|policy|housekeeping}. ...It is jealousy.
You sleep three metres from the only thing I ever wanted. And you snore.
I could make you {guilty|innocent|a toad} without touching the evidence. I want you to know that.
Do you ever wonder why your life is like this? Look up. Wave.
emCapitalBuildup: This court has one sentence left in it that fits you.
I have not used it in {a century|eleven years|a very long time}.
I am going to use it now.
The lesser punishments are for lesser defendants.
You are not a lesser defendant, Em.
You are the reason I keep the old sentences on the books.
Everyone in this room already knows what I am about to say.
Even the ghosts have stopped pretending to write.
emCommuteReasons: Not today. Today it is prison.
Don't ask me why. I am not sure I know.
*the sentence hangs in the air for a long moment*
Do not thank me. It ruins it.
Prison. Get out of my court before I remember why I wanted this.
Killing you would end it, and I am not finished.
Prison. I like knowing where you are.
If you die here, he stops looking for you, and then he has nowhere to be.
Prison. He can visit. He won't. But he can.
emPardonLines: *she looks at the file, then at you, then at the file*
By me. Against me. Whatever the form says.
I said dismissed. Go, before the paperwork catches up.
I have read the evidence twice and found it {boring|unconvincing|beneath me}.
This changes nothing between us. Obviously.
The court is aware that this is the {third|fourth|sixth} time.
The court has told itself to stop counting.
Not to a cell. Home. The one with the {engine|bad suspension|radio that only gets one station}.
emRelapseLines: I was going to let this go. Then you {breathed|blinked|stood there} and I changed my mind.
Do not mistake last time for a pattern. Guilty.
I am allowed to be two things at once. Today I am the other one.
erisWarmthLines: *she reads the name on the file, and reads it again more slowly*
The court notes that it {knows|has met|has had dinner with} the defendant. The court is not going to elaborate.
Strike that from the record. Strike the way I said it, particularly.
Everyone is going to pretend they did not notice that. Everyone.
I am {perfectly|entirely|professionally} impartial. Ask anyone. Do not ask anyone.
You are not going to use this against me. You are, aren't you.
*for the length of one heartbeat she is not a judge at all*
erisClemencyLines: Do not thank me in front of the stenographer.
The court finds a {procedural|evidentiary|clerical} defect in the file.
The defect is that I do not want to do this today.
\C[3]Not guilty. Get out before the paperwork notices.\C[0]
*she puts it back on the bench, carefully, the right way up*
That is twice now. Do not make it a habit. Make it a habit.
Four billion trials this morning and I am {distracted|slow|unforgivably soft} in exactly one of them.
I could convict you standing on my head.
Go home. Take the long way. I like watching.
erisColdSnapLines: Do not look at me like that. It does not work in here.
Whatever you think last time bought you, it did not buy you this.
I am the bench first and everything else a very long way second. Guilty.
One dinner. One. And you thought that was a key.

benevolent: An advocate! How {quaint|charming|touchingly optimistic}. Sit at the little table.
You brought counsel. Nobody brings counsel. I have had that table dusted specially.
Very well. Speak when it helps them and not once when it does not.
neutral: Counsel for the defence. Noted. Do not make me regret noting it.
The court recognises the advocate. Provisionally.
You may address the bench. Address it briefly.
irritated: A lawyer. Wonderful. This will take {twice|four times|an eternity} as long.
I have read your submissions. I read them in the corridor. I read them badly.
Say something useful in the next sentence or sit down.
chaotic: A LAWYER! I have not had one of those in {years|centuries|this dimension}!
Argue at me! Go on! I have no idea what I will do with it!
Rules of evidence? In here? Oh, this is going to be fun for one of us.
vindictive: So you brought a professional. You think I can be argued out of it.
Counsel. Look at me. Now look at your client. One of you is leaving happy.
I have eaten better advocates than you for {breakfast|procedural reasons|no reason at all}.
whimsical: Ooh, a proper lawyer! With the little folder and everything!
Do the thing! The 'objection' thing! I want to hear it done properly!
I shall pretend to be persuadable. It is a wonderful game.
bored: Counsel. Fine. At least somebody in this room has prepared.
Talk. Genuinely, please talk. Anything is better than the silence.
A lawyer. The one thing that makes these longer AND more interesting.
dramatic: AN ADVOCATE STANDS BEFORE THE BENCH! THE OLD FORMS ARE OBSERVED!
SPEAK, CHAMPION OF THE ACCUSED! LET THE RECORD RING WITH IT!

lawyerPartyGreetings: Your {friend|companion|travelling associate} is going to argue for you. In my court. Out loud.
No bar admission. No robe. No shame. Very well, speak.
I see. The defence is somebody who already likes you. How rigorous.
You could have hired a professional. You brought {a friend|company|the person who carries your bags}.
lawyerAbsentLines: No counsel. Good. Fewer people to interrupt me.
You are defending yourself. Bold. Statistically {catastrophic|unwise|very brief}.
The chair for the defence is empty. It usually is. It suits the room.
Nobody speaks for you today. Nobody ever really does.
lawyerBanLines: Stop.
Counsel is {excused|disbarred|removed}.
Not for anything said. For the face that was going to say it.
*the little table is no longer there*
No.
I have decided I do not want to be argued with today.
The defence is struck. The defendant may {continue alone|stand there quietly|reflect}.
Objection.
Mine. To you.
Sustained. Get out of my court.
*somewhere, a filing cabinet acquires a new lawyer*
Are you reading me case law?
In here? To me?
\C[2]Removed.\C[0] I wrote the case law. Badly, on purpose.
I am told you are very good.
That is precisely the problem.
Escort counsel out. Gently. Gently-ish.
*she looks at the advocate for a long, unblinking moment*
You have a {clever|honest|expensive} face and I am not in the mood for any of the three.
Dismissed. Not the case. You.
lawyerObjections: "Objection. The exhibit was recovered from a place that does not exist."
"My client has no memory of the events, which the prosecution has not disputed, because there is no prosecution."
"With respect, the court cited a case it decided by coin toss."
"The charge sheet is dated {tomorrow|the wrong century|in pencil}."
"I would ask the bench to note that my client has been sitting quietly for the entire hearing."
"There is no complainant. There is no witness. There is a pigeon."
"The bounty was calculated by a system the court itself has called insane."
"My client pleads context, Your Honour. Enormous amounts of context."
"Every element of this offence requires intent. My client rarely has any."
"I have prepared eleven authorities. I will read {one|two|none} of them, out of mercy."
lawyerErisReplies: Overruled. {Beautifully argued|Nicely done|Good try} and overruled.
Sustained. Do not look so pleased.
I am writing that down. I am not going to read it back.
The court will pretend it did not hear that, and will remember it forever.
You are {good|expensive|wasted here}. It will not be enough. It might be enough.
*she does not answer for slightly too long*

benevolent.open: I shall try to be... understanding. Try.
benevolent.guilty: Even in all my mercy, I cannot ignore this.
benevolent.innocent: Go on then. I choose kindness today.

neutral.open: Let's keep this simple and fair.
neutral.guilty: The facts leave me no choice.
neutral.innocent: The facts do not support guilt.

irritated.innocent: Fine, innocent. Just get out of my sight.

chaotic.open: Let's see where the dice of fate roll today!
chaotic.innocent: Innocent! Or is it?! Who can say!

vindictive.open: Finally, someone else sits where I usually judge from.
vindictive.guilty: Of course they're guilty. Everyone is.

whimsical.open: Ooh, my turn to play judge! This will be fun!
whimsical.guilty: Guilty! Like a plot twist in a bad play!

bored.innocent: Innocent, I guess. Can I go now?

dramatic.open: BEHOLD! A NEW HAND WIELDS THE GAVEL OF FATE!
dramatic.innocent: INNOCENT! FATE HAS SPOKEN THROUGH ME!

trialSentences: One night in a cell. Think about it.
Three days. One for each time you looked at me like that.
A week. Round numbers comfort me.
Two weeks. I flipped a coin twice.
A month. Long enough to be boring, short enough to survive.
A season. You will come out with a different opinion of weather.
You stay until the debt is paid. Not a minute less.
Your bounty is your sentence. Work it off.
reverseOpeningLines: Court is in session. Try not to bore me.
Stand up straight. I judge posture too.
I have read your file. I was not impressed.
Before we begin, is anyone bringing me wine?
You may speak when spoken to. Rarely, then.
Let the record show that I did not want to be here.
I am the law today. Feel free to panic.
Nice courtroom. I might keep it.
No lawyers. No appeals. Just me.
Smile for the gavel. It likes to be greeted.
reverseOpeningReplies: Your Honor... this is all a misunderstanding.
I did not ask for a divine judge.
Can we please just get this over with?
You are not even a real magistrate.
I have rights, you know. I think.
Everyone said you would be worse.
reversePressApproaches: Ha. And you thought nobody would notice?
Lie to me and you will lose the tongue.
Skip ahead. I have plans tonight.
I could simply read your soul, you know.
reverseClosingLines: I have heard enough. The court will decide.
You have been almost convincing. Almost.
My patience has a floor, and we have reached it.
None of this will matter in a hundred years.
I judge you as I would want to be judged. Frightening, is it not?
The truth is such a small thing. Let us see if I care.
Silence now. The gavel speaks next.
reverseFinalPleas: Whatever you decide, I will remember your face.
Please. I have people waiting for me.
Do what you want. You always do.
This is not justice. It is theatre.
May the gods judge you as you judge me.
reversePartingLines: Court adjourned. Someone clean the floor.
Next case. And bring me that wine.
I hope you understand this was nothing personal.
That was personal, actually. Very personal.
Justice is exhausting. How does anyone do this daily?
Write it in the grimorie. Under 'inevitable'.
I will think about this one tonight. Briefly.
Do not thank me. It ruins the mood.

openings: What a pleasant surprise... or so it seems.
You know, not many have the courage to appear before me willingly.
Or perhaps you were... convinced? Ah, the details!
Today I feel particularly... how should I put it...
Well, let's not exaggerate. But it could be worse for you!
You see, I used to be a goddess of discord...
But now I'm the Goddess of Justice!
Ironic, isn't it? Still makes me laugh.
openings2: It almost makes me want to respect you.
Another pathetic mortal who thinks they can get away with it...
You know what amuses me about you people?
You're all the same. Boring. Guilty.
Ah, look who we have here.
Did you really think you could escape me?
Did you think your crimes would go unnoticed?
openings3: A trial! A glorious, wonderful TRIAL!
Or wait... is it a birthday party?
No no, it's definitely a trial.
Welcome! Or should I say... goodbye?
They're all the same if you think about it enough!
Or was it a game? Let's play anyway!
openings4: You know what? I like you already!
So full of... guilt? Hope? Fear?
I have NO idea what I'm doing!
It would ruin my whole divine image!
It's like monopoly, but with more arbitrary verdicts!
